arxiv-1610-05418.title: Analysis of the semileptonic decay Λ c → n ​ e + ​ ν e \Lambda_{c}\rightarrow ne^{+}\nu_{e}
arxiv-1610-05418.creator: Cheng-Fei Li 1 , Yong-Lu Liu 1 , Ke Liu 1 , Chun-Yu Cui 2 , and Ming-Qiu Huang 1
arxiv-1610-05418.description: Abstract The semileptonic weak decay process of the Λ c \Lambda_{c} baryon to the neutron Λ c → n ​ e + ​ ν e \Lambda_{c}\rightarrow ne^{+}\nu_{e} is examined. The transition form factors are investigated with light-cone QCD sum rules. The differential decay width is obtained in the dynamical region by fitting the sum rules-allowed results with the dipole formula.

arxiv-2303-11428.title: Lamarr: LHCb ultra-fast simulation based on machine learning models deployed within Gauss
arxiv-2303-11428.creator: Matteo Barbetti on behalf of the LHCb Simulation Project
arxiv-2303-11428.description: Abstract About 90% of the computing resources available to the LHCb experiment has been spent to produce simulated data samples for Run 2 of the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. The upgraded LHCb detector will be able to collect larger data samples, requiring many more simulated events to analyze the data to be collected in Run 3.

arxiv-2305-06394.title: Local Region-to-Region Mapping-based Approach to Classify Articulated Objects Thanks: This work was supported by the UK National Centre for Nuclear Robotics (NCNR). Part funded by CHIST-ERA under Project EP/S032428/1 PeGRoGAM and in part supported by Faraday Institution sponsored Recycling of Lithiu
arxiv-2305-06394.creator: Ayush Aggarwal ∗ , Rustam Stolkin, Naresh Marturi
arxiv-2305-06394.description: Abstract Autonomous robots operating in real-world environments encounter a variety of objects that can be both rigid and articulated in nature. Having knowledge of these specific object properties not only helps in designing appropriate manipulation strategies but also aids in developing reliable tracking and pose estimation techniques for many robotic and vision applications.

arxiv-2311-02490.title: Improved Convergence Rates of Windowed Anderson Acceleration for Symmetric Fixed-Point Iterations
arxiv-2311-02490.creator: Casey Garner Gilad Lerman Teng Zhang
arxiv-2311-02490.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Casey Garner Gilad Lerman Teng Zhang. This paper studies the commonly utilized windowed Anderson acceleration (AA) algorithm for fixed-point methods, x ( k + 1 ) = q ⁡ ( x ( k ) ) x^{(k+1)}=q(x^{(k)}) . It provides the first proof that when the operator q q is linear and symmetric the windowed AA, which uses a sliding window of prior iterates, improves the root-linear convergence factor over the fixed-point iterations.

arxiv-2410-01743.title: The Ehrhart h ∗ h^{*} -polynomials of positroid polytopes
arxiv-2410-01743.creator: Yuhan Jiang
arxiv-2410-01743.description: Abstract . A positroid is a matroid realized by a matrix such that all maximal minors are non-negative. Positroid polytopes are matroid polytopes of positroids. In particular, they are lattice polytopes. The Ehrhart polynomial of a lattice polytope counts the number of integer points in the dilation of that polytope.

arxiv-2501-16748.title: Through the Prism of Culture: Evaluating LLMs’ Understanding of Indian Subcultures and Traditions
arxiv-2501-16748.creator: Garima Chhikara, Abhishek Kumar, Abhijnan Chakraborty
arxiv-2501-16748.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Garima Chhikara, Abhishek Kumar, Abhijnan Chakraborty. Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable advancements but also raise concerns about cultural bias, often reflecting dominant narratives at the expense of under-represented subcultures. In this study, we evaluate the capacity of LLMs to recognize and accurately respond to the Little Traditions within Indian society, encompassing localized cultural practices and social institutions such as caste, kinship, marriage, and religion.

arxiv-2507-22532.title: Antiferromagnetic Order and Magnetic Frustration in the Honeycomb Heavy-Fermion System Ce(Pt 1-x Pd x ) 6 Al 3 : 27 Al and 195 Pt NMR Studies
arxiv-2507-22532.creator: Shunsaku Kitagawa 1,, Fumiya Hori 1,, Kenji Ishida 1, Ryohei Oishi 2,, Yasuyuki Shimura 2, Takahiro Onimaru 2, and Toshiro Takabatake 2
arxiv-2507-22532.description: Abstract Heavy-fermion systems with magnetic frustration offer a rich platform for investigating the interplay among Kondo screening, magnetic frustration, and quantum criticality. We report comprehensive 27 Al and 195 Pt nuclear magnetic resonance measurements on polycrystalline Ce(Pt 1-x Pd x ) 6 Al 3 ( x = 0 x=0 , 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3).

arxiv-2509-14834.title: LLM Agents at the Roundtable: A Multi-Perspective and Dialectical Reasoning Framework for Essay Scoring
arxiv-2509-14834.creator: Jinhee Jang, Ayoung Moon, Minkyoung Jung, YoungBin Kim, Seung Jin Lee
arxiv-2509-14834.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jinhee Jang, Ayoung Moon, Minkyoung Jung, YoungBin Kim, Seung Jin Lee. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has brought a new paradigm to automated essay scoring (AES), a long-standing and practical application of natural language processing in education. However, achieving human-level multi-perspective understanding and judgment remains a challenge. In this work, we propose Roundtable Essay Scoring (RES), a multi-agent evaluation framework designed to perform precise and human-aligned scoring under a zero-shot setting.

pmc-10554837.title: THU597 Po2-guided Adrenal Vein Sampling In Primary Aldosteronism
pmc-10554837.creator: Kei Omata, Yuta Tezuka, Yoshikiyo Ono, Fumitoshi Satoh
pmc-10554837.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Background: Accurate laterality diagnosis of adrenal aldosterone over-secretion is crucial in determining specific treatment for primary aldosteronism. Although adrenal vein sampling (AVS) is considered as the gold standard method for lateralization, successful canulation to right adrenal vein (RAV) has been reported to be difficult since RAV usually empties directly into inferior vena cava (IVC).

pmc-10647432.title: Amyloid Fibrils Produced by Streptococcus sanguinis Contribute to Biofilm Formation and Immune Evasion
pmc-10647432.creator: Eduardo M Franco, Lívia A Alves, Hassan Naveed, Victor A A Freitas, Débora C Bastos, Renata O Mattos-Graner, Babak Baban, Divyashri Baraniya
pmc-10647432.description: Bacterial surface proteins assembled into amyloids contribute to biofilm formation and host immune evasion. Streptococcus sanguinis, a pioneer colonizer of teeth commonly involved in cardiovascular infections, expresses about thirty-three proteins anchored to the cell wall by sortase A. Here, we characterized the production of amyloid in S.

pmc-12557148.title: Sexual orientation differences in ACEs and internalizing psychopathology: Swedish population study
pmc-12557148.creator: BD Smart, R Bränström, JE Pachankis
pmc-12557148.description: BackgroundSexual minority (SM) populations experience increased risk of mental health problems compared to heterosexuals, yet the role of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) remains understudied. This study's research questions were: (1) What ACE differences exist based on sexual orientation? (2) Can any elevated ACE exposure be explained by SM groups’ greater gender non-conformity (GNC)?

pmc-12612506.title: Reliability of Preoperative Magnetic Resonance Imaging in Determining the Anterior Cruciate Ligament Tear Location
pmc-12612506.creator: Andre Yanuar, Calvin Calvin, Rani Maria, Miftakhul Jannah Kurniawati, Ghuna Arioharjo Utoyo
pmc-12612506.description: Background:The accurate identification of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear location is important for preoperative planning, as it influences the choice between reconstruction or repair procedures, particularly for proximal tears. Therefore, there is a need for a reliable preoperative tool that yields findings consistent with diagnostic arthroscopy.

pmc-12989442.title: The Chloride Channel Regulator, Calcium-Activated-1 Is Expressed in Synoviocytes and Articular Chondrocytes in Health and Disease
pmc-12989442.creator: Judith Bushe, Jenny Fürstenau, Florian Bartenschlager, Simon Dökel, Vladimir M. Jovanovic, Gundula Rösch, Zsuzsa Jenei-Lanzl, Frank Zaucke, Kristina Dietert, Achim D. Gruber
pmc-12989442.description: The chloride channel regulator, calcium-activated-1, CLCA1, acts as a multifunctional secreted glycoprotein in anion channel modulation, mucus homeostasis, immune regulation, and other functions. So far, it has been described in goblet and other mucus-producing cells in mucous membranes, primarily of the respiratory, alimentary, and urogenital tracts.

pmc-13206537.title: Hyperreflective Foci in the Inner Nuclear Layer: Proof‐of‐Concept for an Optical Coherence Tomography Derived Microglia‐Related Marker in Multiple Sclerosis
pmc-13206537.creator: Jonathan A. Gernert, Laura M. Bartos, Tara Christmann, Hanna Zausinger, Luca N. Diedrich, Daniel Engels, Miriam Schlüter, Sarah Schlaeger, Sophia Stoecklein, Leonie F. Keidel, Tania Kümpfel, Martin Kerschensteiner, Matthias Brendel, Joachim Havla
pmc-13206537.description: The role of microglia has emerged as a critical driver of disease progression in multiple sclerosis (MS), but we lack broadly applicable monitoring tools. Here, we investigated whether hyperreflective foci (HRF), as detected by optical coherence tomography (OCT) within the inner nuclear layer (INL) of the retina, can be used as a marker for microglial pathology.

pmc-13303339.title: Exploring the Functional Impact of Individual DDX41 Variants With a Fast and Robust Cell‐Based Method
pmc-13303339.creator: Nikolaj Juul Nitschke, Marwa Almosailleakh, Issa Ismail Issa, Clara Amanda Skov, Casper Carstens Lund, Jakob Werner Hansen, Jakob Schmidt Jespersen, Klas Raaschou-Jensen, Claudia Schöllkopf, Marianne Tang Severinsen, Bo Porse, Joachim Weischenfeld, Anne Stidsholt Roug, Mette Klarskov Andersen, Morte
pmc-13303339.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Germline DDX41 variants are found in up to 4% of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDSs), with a higher prevalence among males and a late onset. In this study, we analyzed 647 Danish patients with suspected myeloid neoplasms to assess the frequency of germline DDX41 variants and the functional impact of variants of uncertain significance (VUSs) using a cell‐based assay, CRISPR‐Select.

pmc-13361788.title: Characteristics of COVID-19 cases and factors associated with disease severity in Lao People’s Democratic Republic: a nationwide study
pmc-13361788.creator: Souphatsone Houatthongkham, Phonepadith Xangsayarath, Bouaphanh Khamphaphongphane, Souphalak Inthaphatha, Ai Aoki, Kimihiro Nishino, Eiko Yamamoto
pmc-13361788.description: ObjectivesThis is the first nationwide analysis to describe the epidemiological and clinical characteristics of COVID-19 cases in Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) and to identify factors associated with symptom-based disease severity during the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic in Lao PDR.

pmc-13648135.title: Sinonasal hemangiosarcoma following juvenile occupational exposure to formaldehyde when breeding farm animals
pmc-13648135.creator: Daniela Napolitano, Stefania Massacesi, Roberto Calisti
pmc-13648135.description: BackgroundHemangiosarcomas are heterogeneous malignancies possibly originating in any part of the body, rare in humans. The web of causation of human hemangiosarcomas remains poorly understood, to date, except for subsets of cases which have been recognized in a well-defined causal correlation to vinyl chloride or to ionizing radiation.

pmc-13672134.title: Silicon Photonic Beam Steerer Based on Metalens Focal Plane Array
pmc-13672134.creator: Chung‐Yu Hsu, Ping‐Yen Hsieh, Hsun‐Sung Chiu, Li‐Jun Tung, Chieh‐Chih Yu, Ko‐Chi Chen, Yu‐Heng Hong, Hao‐Chung Kuo, Chi‐Wai Chow, You‐Chia Chang
pmc-13672134.description: Focal plane arrays (FPAs) promise robust solid‐state beam steering for LiDAR and free‐space optical communications. However, the need for external collimation lenses hinders chip‐scale compactness. Discrete switching between FPA elements further introduces blind spots and limits the number of resolvable points, restricting applications that require continuous tracking.

pmc-13677447.title: Plant–Soil Feedbacks May Underlie Competitive Dynamics Between Co‐Occurring Invasive Annual Grasses Bromus tectorum and Ventenata dubia
pmc-13677447.creator: Lilly Sencenbaugh, Jane M. Mangold, Bruce D. Maxwell, Danielle E. M. Ulrich, Lisa J. Rew
pmc-13677447.description: Plant communities are shaped by interactions among plants and soil legacies. Plant–soil feedbacks (PSF) may alter invasion dynamics and change plant community species composition. There have been field observations of the invasive annual grass, Ventenata dubia , replacing another invasive annual grass, Bromus tectorum , though previous work has not found evidence of competition that would support these shifts.
